topic: llama.cpp shipped b12186, b12187 and b12188 inside one day -- re-pin and re-measure
title: llama.cpp has no stable release
description: llama.cpp ships continuously: three builds landed inside one hour. Working description; the package stage writes the final one.
hook_candidates: Three llama.cpp releases in one hour. Yours is older.
There is no stable llama.cpp. There never was.
llama.cpp shipped six builds before you finished lunch.
Your llama.cpp build has a birthday. It was weeks ago.
No stable llama.cpp release exists. The maintainer said so.
Six llama.cpp builds before noon. Count yours.
Your llama.cpp is three releases behind as of breakfast.
One hour, three llama.cpp releases, zero pings to you.
Waiting for stable llama.cpp? The answer was not atm.
Re-pin llama.cpp tonight or drift quietly behind.
narration_full: There is no stable llama.cpp. There never was. You are waiting anyway; the maintainer: not at the moment. You downloaded a build weeks ago and cannot say which number. Nothing pings you; your copy drifts. Today stamped six releases; three inside one hour, eleven eleven to eleven fifty-eight. Each build is one named change: a Vulkan fix, a WebGPU kernel, a server scheduling fix. Each ships forty prebuilt downloads. Never measured? Then pinning costs nothing you can see. No upstream speed number exists, so yours comes from llama-bench, the tool that counts your tokens per second. Tonight: check, re-pin, re-run llama-bench. Old row, new row: the update is a number, not a vibe.
